$comment: PipelineK SDK pin lockfile (R-22, audit 2026-10-10; R5.4 sweep 2026-10-12).
$schema_doc: Each entry pins an SDK release to the SHA-256 of the canonical jar AND
the SHA-256 of the official distribution ZIP. The studio probe computes
the jar SHA at boot and refuses to admit runs if it does not match
(when STUDIO_SDK_PIN=enforce, the default for non-dev runs). The cert
harness verifies the ZIP SHA + per-jar SHAs before extracting.
To add a new pin:
1. Download the SDK ZIP from the official release page; record its
SHA-256 with `sha256sum`.
2. Extract it; compute the SHA-256 of pipeline-application-X.Y.Z.jar
with `sha256sum`.
3. Add an entry with both exact lowercase hex strings.
The lockfile is loaded once at boot; the SHAs reported via /api/version
are the ones the probe + cert computed at runtime. Operators compare
the two to detect silent SDK drift.
R5.4 (2026-10-12): `version` is now the jar's MANIFEST.MF
Implementation-Version (what the probe reads at runtime), NOT the
GitHub release tag. The official 0.48.0-rc1 build carries
Implementation-Version=0.48.0, so the lockfile's `version` is 0.48.0
and the GitHub release tag is recorded separately in `releaseTag`.
This way the probe can match the manifest version to the lockfile
without forcing a lockfile maintainer to invent data.

pinned_sdks._comment_zip: C1.1 (2026-10-12): the ZIP pin is part of the cert resolver contract (ZipSdkResolver). The canonical jar pin (sha256) remains the source of truth at runtime; the ZIP pin lets a fresh clone verify the dist before extracting any jar.
